newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ACTU ATTACKS GOVERNMENT ON UNEMPLOYMENT
The ACTU says the Federal Government has failed to produce any long term initiatives to reduce unemployment and, in many cases, is eroding job security for many Australians.
It's dimissed the Government's eight-per cent unemployment target for the year ahead as impossible to achieve on economic growth projections.

ACTU President Jennie George says an annual economic growth rate of up to four-and-a-half per cent is needed to attack unemployment, but the Treasurer hasn't set his sights that high. Ms George says the Government's prediction of three-and-three quarter per cent growth won't be enough to address the problem.
PM DOESN'T COMPLETELY RULE OUT STEEL RIVER TRADE ZONE
The Prime Minister says there are constitutional difficulties associated with setting up a defered trade zone in Newcastle.
John Howard yesterday announced his plan to help the Hunter in the wake of BHP's decision to quit steelmaking in 1999, matching New South Wales Premier Bob Carr's 10-million dollar commitment.
The Prime Minister says he wants to talk to business leaders and unions about how to spend the money.
And while not completely ruling out the move, Mr Howard has told ABC Radio he may not be able to approve the constitutional changes needed for the proposed steel river trade zone.
He says under the constitution, the Government can't discriminate in its tax measures between states or different parts of states.
WILLIAMS BACK IN COURT TODAY
Carlton star Greg Williams heads back to the Supreme Court today, in his fight against a nine-week suspension, which could stretch into tomorrow.
Williams and Carlton claim the charge of unduly interfering with an umpire was wrongly laid, and wrongly heard by the AFL Tribunal.
They also claim they would suffer considerable financial loss if the suspension is upheld ... Carlton says it could lose almost one and a half million dollars if it misses the finals.
For its part, the defence claims the matter was handled within the rules of the AFL.
ACOSS SAYS BUDGET OFFERS DISTANT CARROT TO UNEMPLOYED
The Australian Council of Social Service says Peter Costello has produced a budget for the better-off while offering only a distant carrot to the unemployed.
Representative Robert Fitzgerald says the billion-dollar Centenary Fund won't even start for another year, while money's cut out of public housing.
Mr Fitzgerald says it's disgraceful and extraordinary that three-point five billion dollars is allocated for tax incentives on savings which will largely go to the better off.
But he says the Government can't afford to house people properly and is cutting public housing.
AMA SAYS A BILLION DOLLARS CUT FROM HEALTH CARE
Federal president of the Australian Medical Association Keith Woollard says the Budget appears to have taken a billion dollars out of health care.

Dr Woollard says general practice has taken the biggest hit. He says the minister has said that GPs will only get half the increase in rebates available to their patients, as would be justified by the increase in costs.
Dr Woollard says this means it's going to be almost impossible for GPs to continue to sustain the quality of health care that they provide for the community.
